description: Gripper Gen 11, Astra pass: a GPT-6 Astra refinement of Opus 5.5's Gen 11 yellow fingers (follow-up from voice-6663a540; Jake: 'Once Opus 5.5 finishes it, we can give it to Astra for a pass as well.'). Copy 'Two Finger Gripper/versions/v011_generalist_fingers_opus' to a NEW folder v011b_generalist_fingers_astra and work only there, so Gen 11 Opus and Gen 11 Astra both stay viewable. Read its README.md and rounds/*/round.json first. The reference photos cad/reference/generalist_gripper_gen6_*.png are the source of truth. Keep Jake's asks: (1) the inner-face ridges are very shallow grooves, about 0.5 to 1 mm deep, cut straight across the full width of the gripping face and finely spaced; (2) skinny, pointed tips; (3) every hole goes through (genus.py must pass); (4) a working open/close slider and rotation in the gallery: add a cad/mobile_gallery/poses.js entry (the pivot is gripper.scad 'pivot'; Scripts/test_gripper_poses.py checks it) and a name in Scripts/publish_designs.py generations. Points the Opus reviewer left open: one plain band at the inside corner below the beak's shoulder; side.png may show the beak tapering from the outer side only, like a chisel (low confidence). Build/review loop with a separate reviewer, up to 3 rounds.

results.identified_issue: side.png was read as a near-plan (dorsal) view because the slot row and dot appear near the jaw edge; the reviewer agreed. If that's wrong, the edge-on taper should be one-sided instead. NEEDLE_CHISEL=(0.77,0.9) eases only the outer edge (k=1) with a cubic up to the knee, then makes it linear to the tip. The jaw edge (A=1.31) is untouched, and its convexity gives a slight raptor-beak lean the reviewer noted. Easing the knee to ~0.80 is the next lever. RIDGE_TIP_CLEAR_PX=8 was needed because the fuller beak let a 30th groove past RIDGE_MIN_WIDTH_PX, and it made a pinhole (genus 34). The Opus v011 poses.js pivot was corrected 27.359→27.672: its gripper.scad echoes 27.6719 and test_hinges_match_the_scad failed on it. test_gripper_poses' regex is now v\d+[a-z]? so v011b doesn't resolve to the v011 folder. The remaining test failure, 'hinge ^Right moves no part', comes from the published catalog in ~/HelpingHands-tools: it holds a single assembly model whenever the part STLs are older than the scad deps at publish time. serve_designs.py was live and republishing during my edits. Scripts/publish_designs.py is untracked in this checkout (pre-existing). It got the '11b' generation plus a gen_{number:0>2} format so a string label works, and that edit is uncommitted.
results.summary: Gen 11b is up next to Gen 11: the beak now ends in a straight chamfer like the photos. GPT-6 Astra was unavailable, so Opus 5.5 did this pass.
results.detailed_description:
Heads up first: this pebble asked for GPT-6 Astra (codex), but that was unavailable, so the work fell back to Claude Opus 5.5. That means this is a second Opus pass, not an Astra one. It lives in its own folder, v011b_generalist_fingers_astra, and shows in the gallery as Gen 11b next to Gen 11.

The two open questions turned out simpler than they looked. side.png is a top-down view: you can tell because the slot row and black dot sit near the gripping edge, just like in the two-hands photo. So the 'chisel' is the beak's outline seen from above. The gripping edge runs straight to the nub. The outer edge stays full, then breaks at a knee into one flat facet. I changed only that: the outer edge stays full out to 77% of the way from the dot to the point, then runs straight to the point. The thickness taper seen edge-on stays even on both sides. The plain band at the inside corner was already gone in Opus's r4: the grooves start right at the shoulder.

The grooves are unchanged: 0.5 mm deep, 1 mm apart, straight across the full width of the jaw. They now stop 1.6 mm short of the point, because the fuller beak let in one more groove at the tip and it broke through as a pinhole. All 33 holes go through, each finger is one watertight body, and the fingers don't collide anywhere from 0 to 30°. A separate reviewer did two rounds: a1 scored 7.5 (it still read as one smooth curve) and a2 scored 8, ship it. compare.html shows every round over the photo.

Gallery: I added a poses.js entry so the open/close slider works for Gen 11b. Gen 11 Opus's entry had a stale pivot (27.359 mm; the real value is 27.672 mm), so I fixed that too. I also fixed the pose test, which was checking the wrong folder for 11b.

Two things I couldn't finish. The 'Gen 11b' name in Scripts/publish_designs.py is in place, but that file is untracked in this checkout and isn't mine, so it isn't committed. Please commit it. Also, the published gallery currently shows Gen 11 Opus as one merged model, which is why its open/close slider doesn't move the fingers. A fresh publish should fix that.

summary: Copy Gen 11 Opus yellow fingers into a new v011b_generalist_fingers_astra folder and refine them there, using the gen6 reference photos as truth. Keep the shallow full-width grooves, skinny pointed tips and through-holes, add the gallery pose and publish entries, and resolve the open beak-corner and chisel-taper questions.
